newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil hikes spending despite cost-cuts plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil hikes spending despite cost-cuts plan - paper.

text.p: The Brazilian government has authorized an additional 1.9 billion reais ($1.86 billion) in spending, just three days after unveiling a fiscal package to curb federal expenses, Folha de S. Paulo newspaper said.

The paper said President Fernando Henrique Cardoso issued a decree, published Monday in the official gazette, that reduces by more than a third some 5.0 billion reais ($4.9 billion) in budget cuts set out in June.

The extra spending in the 1996 federal budget is for investments and maintenance of public entities, which the government argued was needed to balance revenues with the volume of expenses, Folha said.
